content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"pass","note":"The decision ties specific evidence (no receipts, no medical notes on cause, affidavits, Complainant's own testimony that financial trouble began in 2019) to its denial of pecuniary damages and its non-pecuniary finding, so the reasoning can be reconstructed from the record, although the $25,000 figure is supported only by general reference to case law."},"rc2":{"status":"pass","note":"Characterizations are attributed to identifiable sources such as Complainant's affidavit, statements from his wife, sister and mother, the 'Note From Hawaii Pacific Health,' the photograph, and the cited Israel F. decision."},"rc3":{"status":"pass","note":"The chronology is dated and followable: June–December 2020 events, the December 21, 2020 counseling, the December 30, 2020 formal complaint, the August 17, 2021 FAD, the August 17, 2023 EEOC decision, and the October 10, 2023 ROI, though the AWOL is described as a date and as 1.3 hours in October."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The record shows what the Agency considered and the criteria applied (causation, exacerbation, non-compensability of EEO process distress, similar awards), but it does not identify who made the decision, and the derivation of the $25,000 figure and the sum to $26,500 is only loosely explained."},"rc5":{"status":"review","note":"The record is largely self-contained for evaluating the damages denial, but the unnamed decision-maker, the thin explanation for the award amount, the removed case numbers, and the unspecified date of the final decision require some outside context for a fully independent assessment."}}}
